_doc: Anti-drift compass for the HIVE DEEPWALK EXPANSION arc (Ian 2026-07-27: 'I love this flow we just had in marketplace'). Companion to HIVE_DEEPWALK_EXPANSION_ROADMAP.md. tools/hive_deepwalk_scoreboard.py reads this and emits a MEASURED % per phase and per HK class. EXPANSION means growing BOTH denominators: journeys x personas x states (board 1) and new HK dimension classes (board 2). A cell moves only on cited live evidence.
_phases_def: ground - map the views, transitions and the caches each one touches
walk - live-MCP journey walk carrying the full lens; requires >=2 personas AND >=2 states
observe - record friction with evidence (a clean walk is a real result, record it as such)
harvest - Engine B, at spoke 5 ONLY, for a friction the walk actually surfaced
resolve - fix, then LOCK with a gate; a fix without a gate is not done
_coverage_rule: A journey's W phase is 'done' only when walked in >=2 personas AND >=2 states. One-persona/one-state is the shallowness this arc exists to kill.

H1-first-run-onboard-choice.notes: view-onboard: create vs join. Grounded 2026-07-27: the 7 views exist (onboard/create/code/join/welcome/board/shell).

H2-create-hive-become-owner.notes: view-create -> hives.insert -> owner membership -> view-welcome -> view-board.

H3-join-by-code-valid.notes: view-join / view-code -> hive_members.upsert -> welcome. P-invited is the persona that has never been walked.

H4-join-by-code-invalid.notes: S-error: bad code / expired / already a member. Does each say which it is, or one generic failure?

H5-board-first-paint-by-role.notes: 2026-07-27 walked as christinedizon (worker): board renders, supervisor panel hidden and EMPTY (see HK1). Owed: supervisor + owner personas, and S-single-member. | 2026-07-27 completed via the H10 switch: the SAME user was walked as worker (Manila) and supervisor (Lucena), which is a stronger comparison than two different accounts because only the role differs. Worker: supervisor panel hidden and EMPTY. Supervisor: visible and FILLED (20 / 4 / 0 / 65), and documentElement carries is-supervisor.

H6-invite-and-code-lifecycle.notes: Code generation + regeneration. Does regenerating invalidate the old code immediately?

H7-change-member-role.notes: hive_members.update. Does the demoted member's OPEN SESSION lose the affordances, or only after reload?

H8-remove-member.notes: hive_members.delete. THE REVOCATION QUESTION: what does P-removed still hold client-side and still render? Drive-order item 1.

H9-leave-hive.notes: performLeave() + the audit-log ordering already hardened 2026-07-07 (audit BEFORE self-delete). Walk it end to end: where does the user land?

H10-switch-hive.notes: WAS UNWALKABLE BY CONSTRUCTION until 2026-07-27 (see HK2): seeded data was strictly 1:1 worker->hive so the switcher list was always length 1. Seeder now creates one P-multi worker with a DIFFERENT role in the second hive, so the switch is observable. R=partial: the fixture is fixed, the walk is owed. Drive-order item 1. | 2026-07-27 WALKED (first walk of this arc, and it found a real defect). FIXTURE: gave christinedizon a 2nd membership (Lucena Pharmaceutical, role supervisor) alongside Manila Electronics (worker) - the same shape the seeder now produces, so local state matches a post-reseed world. DEFECT FOUND: the switcher listed only ONE hive while the DB had two. Root cause is precise - the if(HIVE_ID) branch re-validates the ACTIVE membership every load (syncs role, clears everything on kicked) but never refreshes the LIST; wh_hives is written at sign-in (index.html) and rebuilt only by recoverHiveMembership(), which runs SOLELY when the user has no active hive. So a membership granted after sign-in - a supervisor adding you to a second plant, a join on another device - stayed invisible until sign-out. Same shape as the identity caches that bit this platform twice: trusted when present, re-derived only when absent. FIXED: reconcileHiveList() now runs on every board load (one bounded query against v_worker_truth + v_hives_truth, the same views the recovery path uses; best-effort so it never blocks the board; preserves any invite code already held since the truth view does not carry it). VERIFIED LIVE end to end: both hives now listed with correct per-hive roles, active hive unchanged (no disruption), and the SWITCH itself re-derives all three caches together - id b4f7fe63->4eec150e, name Manila->Lucena, and critically role worker->supervisor rather than carrying the old role across.

H11-hive-settings-rename.notes: hives.update. Does a rename propagate to wh_hive_name and every surface showing it?

H12-member-list-and-presence.notes: 'ON SHIFT NOW / Green dot = a teammate is in WorkHive right now' observed rendering 2026-07-27. Owed: is the presence signal BACKED by a live producer, or decorative? (the MK1 producer test, applied here).

H13-hive-health-maturity.notes: 2026-07-27: the panel ships to a worker as template only, 'Computing hive health...', zero filled values. Owed: walk as supervisor and apply the producer test to every number it shows.

H14-cross-surface-hive-identity.notes: A switch or removal must be correct on EVERY page reading whHiveId(), not just the board that changed it. Cache set grounded 2026-07-27: wh_hive_id, wh_hive_name, wh_hive_role, wh_active_hive_id, wh_hives, wh_hive_lastseen_<id>. Drive-order item 1.

HK1-boundary-is-real-not-cosmetic.seed: A role/tenancy boundary must be enforced by DATA (RLS or a server-derived role), never by CSS visibility alone. A hidden element must be EMPTY, not display:none over real data.
HK1-boundary-is-real-not-cosmetic.notes: 2026-07-27 SWEEP (partial, one page): hive.html PASSES with a caveat. #supervisor-summary is present in a worker's DOM (9,699 chars) behind class='hidden', but contains TEMPLATE ONLY - zero filled numeric nodes. Then the stronger probe: forging wh_hive_role to 'supervisor' in localStorage and reloading, the page OVERWROTE it back to 'worker' and granted nothing, so the role is server-re-derived. That is the opposite of the marketplace's wh_last_worker/wh_hive_id staleness. CAVEAT driving the detect stage: the pattern is fragile - if a later change fills that panel before checking role, CSS becomes the only thing hiding real data. | 2026-07-27 CONFIRMED BOTH WAYS on the same user across a hive switch, which settles the caveat: as a WORKER the panel is hidden AND contains zero filled values; as a SUPERVISOR it is visible AND filled (20/4/0/65). The data is therefore fetched CONDITIONALLY ON ROLE, not fetched-then-hidden - CSS was never the gate here. Combined with the forged-role probe (wh_hive_role set to supervisor is overwritten back to worker on load, because the if(HIVE_ID) branch re-validates against v_worker_truth), hive.html's role boundary is real on both the data and the identity side. detect/gate still owed: a detector that asserts this stays true, since the failure mode is a future change that fills the panel before checking.

HK2-testability-of-a-built-capability.seed: If the product ships a capability, seeded state must be able to EXERCISE it. A capability no fixture can reach is untested by construction, and its bugs are invisible to every walk and every screenshot.
HK2-testability-of-a-built-capability.notes: 2026-07-27 FOUND + FIXED: seeded data was strictly 1:1 worker->hive (15 memberships / 15 workers / 0 multi-hive) because hives_workers.py built exactly one member_row per worker, while hive.html carries ~28 hive-switcher references. H10 was therefore unwalkable by construction. Fixed in the seeder: one worker now receives a second membership in a different hive with a DIFFERENT role, so the switch is observable rather than merely possible. Same lesson as the marketplace trust columns in a new shape - the SEEDER decides what can be tested; under-generating a relationship is the quieter failure because nothing looks wrong. GATE owed: assert every shipped capability has a fixture that can reach it.
